FRESNO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT

The Fresno County Superior Court is the cornerstone of justice in Fresno, CA, handling criminal, civil, family, traffic, and juvenile cases. Established in 1856 and consolidated in 1998, it serves residents with a mission to ensure fair, timely resolutions and equal access to justice.

Key Details:

  • Address: 1100 Van Ness Ave, Fresno, CA 93724
  • Hours: Mon-Fri 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM | Closed Sat-Sun
  • Website: Fresno County Superior Court
  • Judges: David Andrew Gottlieb, Gregory T. Fain, Houry A. Sanderson, and 11 others.

ourt Services & Case Management

Fresno County Superior Court offers streamlined services to reduce in-person visits:

  • Online Case Search: Search by case number, name, or filing date via the Public Portal.
  • E-Filing & Payments: File documents or pay fines online for traffic, citations, or court fees.
  • Self-Help Resources: Access forms, legal guides, and workshops for family law, small claims, and more.
  • Live Courtroom Streams: Watch proceedings remotely for transparency.

Confidential Records: Some cases (e.g., juvenile, sealed) require in-person requests. Fees apply for archived documents.

Fresno is a city courthouse in Fresno County, California. The Eastern District California appeals go to the United States of Appeals ninth circuit. The courthouse was established in 1856 and was abandoned in 1867. In 1998 the courthouse consolidated municipal and county courts into the Superior Court of Fresno County. fresno county superior court mission is to serve all the county residents and gain the trust and confidence of the public in the administration of justice with proper behavior, timely resolution of disputes, ensuring following of the rules and law and promoting equal access to the courts. fresno has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims, probation, juvenile, civil, family, traffic, and vehicle matters. county superior court provide services like online account payment, forms, online case search, e-filing, live streams of courtrooms and many more notices, so it is optional to go to court for these services. fresno county superior court also provides self-help process for a different division. Every person must follow local rules and wear a mask in this court. Proper dressing is required during the case hearing. Calendar and Daily Hearing can be viewed through the daily master calendar. Six fresno courts located in this county are:

  • FRESNO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – B.F. SISK COURTHOUSE
  • FRESNO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – CRIMINAL COURTS DEPARTMENTS 95 & 96
  • FRESNO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – DOWNTOWN
  • FRESNO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – JUVENILE
  • FRESNO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – M STREET COURTHOUSE
  • FRESNO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT –Action Center

How to search for case information?

fresno county Superior Court Case Search can be done online using the court case management search. The fresno court maintains all the records online, in files or in a database. The Search can be done in the following ways:

  • Search by Case Number, citation or traffic number
  • Search by First, middle and last name
  • Search by Party or business name
  • Search by Filling date
  • Search by Case type

The portal of fresno county superior court will only show those records process information that is publicly available. Some records are unavailable; if the information does not come, the case records will be removed or confidential and cannot be displayed online. people have to go to the court and give a request for these question types of documents, and then the court will decide whether to provide that information to people or not. The fees for each document per page are required. Achieved information is also available for legally maintaining legal records. The cases stored in the archives end are the appellate case, limited and unlimited civil, criminal felonies and misdemeanors, family law and support, juvenile dependency, probate, traffic and small claims matters.

Types of Cases Handled by the Superior Court of fresno county

Fresno County superior court is responsible for handling a wide range of legal cases, including civil, criminal, family law, juvenile, and probate cases. Civil cases notices may involve disputes between individuals or businesses, while criminal cases involve charges of criminal activity. Family law cases involve issues such as divorce, child custody, and support, while juvenile cases involve minors who are accused of criminal activity. Probate cases involve the distribution of a deceased person's assets and debts.

The Judges of the Superior Court of Fresno County

The judges of Fresno County play a critical role in the court operations. To become a judge in the Superior Court of Fresno, an individual must meet certain qualifications, including being a licensed attorney and having experience in the legal field. Judges in the Superior Court of Fresno County are either appointed by the governor or elected by the public. The role of a judge in the Superior Court of Fresno County is to preside over legal cases, make decisions on legal matters, and ensure that court proceedings are conducted fairly and justly.

The Superior Court of Fresno County follows specific procedures for pretrial, trial, and appeal notices proceedings. Pretrial procedures process may include motions and hearings, while trial procedures involve the presentation of evidence and arguments by both sides. Appeal notices procedures involve the review of a lower court decision by a higher court. fresno county superior website provides information on the court procedures, notices and guidelines for each type of case.

fresno county superior court offers a variety of programs and services to the public, including self-help services, alternative dispute resolution programs, and domestic violence services. The court self-help center provides information and resources to individuals who are representing themselves in a legal matter. The domestic violence notices services provide support and resources to individuals who have been affected by domestic violence.

How can I make a payment?

street courthouse fresno county superior court fee payment for traffic tickets and fines can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay fee for tickets and fines in street courthouse fresno court by visiting fresno county superior during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the payment center. Take your ticket when you are coming for payment. 2.5% surcharges will be applied if people make payment with a credit card.

Online

Fresno court online fee payments can be made using the fresno county superior Online Portal https://publicportal.fresno.courts.ca.gov/FRESNOPORTAL/. Enter the Ticket/Citation, case, and driving license number. Your case information with the amount of the fine | fee by law will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online.

Mail

In fresno superior A Person can send a certified fee check or money order to fresno county superior Court's mailing address; Fresno Superior Court ATTN: Traffic Division 1100 Van Ness Avenue Fresno, CA 93724. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number and account number when people send the fee payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if people want a receipt in end.

Telephone

In fresno superior Traffic Tickets can also be made using the telephone by calling and request the traffic department at any time 559-457-1700 during regular business hours.

Extensions in fee payments, for some cases, are also available in fresno superior. The clerk's office gives a 90-day extension to follow or pays bail on some cases in which appearance is not mandatory.

The family court handles which types of cases?

Fresno County Court family law matters are handled by the B.F. Sisk Courthouse. Family law handles and helps people with the following legal issues:

  • Divorce, legal separation or nullity of marriage
  • Child custody and visitation issues
  • Child, Spousal and Family support issues
  • Domestic Violence
  • Elder abuse issue
  • Issues related to marital property division
  • traffic court

The family law clerk will help you understand with some information regarding forms and cases of fresno county superior court, but they cannot provide open legal advice or do not act as an attorney. Contact allowed to the family law facilitator's office for assistance at any time if you cannot afford an attorney.

How to fight a traffic citation?

Fresno County court traffic cases are handled by the M Street Courthouse . You can receive a traffic ticket citation if you do any illegal vehicle or traffic violation like an accident, driving without a license or suspended license and many more in traffic court. If you received a citation, then notice the citation date written on it, and you had to pay or appear in court on this date and time. If your case notice is severe, you must appear on the due date with your attorney to answer; otherwise, write a plea or pay the fine before the due date. If you did nothing and the calling citation date passed, then $100 will be added to your balance because of civil assessment. According to the written declaration under California Vehicle Code 40903, you are doomed to a written declaration trial.

What is the eligibility for remote video proceedings?

Fresno County court traffic court also offers remote video proceedings for traffic cases. The service is only available by those who live 15 miles away from the county M courthouse or are away from the county, and their due date to follow and time is coming. Their citation can be handled by video conferencing. You first had to register and inform the court before the due date for jury duty service.

How to file small claims cases?

Fresno County Court small claims matters are handled by the – B.F. Sisk Courthouse. This court can resolve your matter quickly upon request and inexpensively. The limit for the claim is up to $7500. You can file a small claim in any county court by filing the form available in the clerk's office. Type all your personal information, the defendant's information, the reason and how minor your claim is, and submit or send it to the court. The defendant must be a resident of this county, and the damage or injury must occur in that county; if the person or the injury is not done in this county, then the claim is not filed in this court. You must write a five-page document claim, questions make two copies for each defendant's name and keep one copy with yourself.
